# OwnerFlight — Full Text

OwnerFlight books calls with home care agency owners for businesses that sell into home care — done-for-you outreach backed by a scored database of 2,860 agencies across 24 live states (Pilot Flight $400 one-time, DFY $800/mo, DIY database $299/mo for any 3 states, All-Access $499/mo for every live state, DFY annual prepaid $8,000/year).

The market, measured
The agencies are good. Their visibility isn't.
Every figure below is computed from the live OwnerFlight database — all 2,860 agency records across the 24 live states, October 2026. The denominator is printed next to every number: if a signal wasn't verified on a record, that record isn't counted.
home care agencies tracked across 24 live states

agencies with a verified booking status offer any online booking
The other 1,108 verified agencies take no bookings online at all. The remaining 1,537 records are excluded — booking status not yet verified, never estimated.
1,768 / 1,808
checked agencies have no findable Instagram presence
Social presence checked on 1,808 agencies across 19 states; only 40 publish a findable handle. California and Massachusetts have not been checked yet and are excluded from this figure entirely.

median Google reviews per rated agency
Computed over the 1,125 agencies with a published Google review count. Well-reviewed, barely visible — that gap is what our clients sell into.
The problem
Prospecting should not begin with a scavenger hunt.
Your team’s best hours belong in outreach—not in twelve open tabs trying to verify who runs an agency.
01 / SEARCH
Maps is not a database
Manual searches surface duplicates, franchises, and incomplete profiles. Every city becomes a separate research project.
02 / VERIFY
Licenses take time
Matching businesses to state license records and decision-makers turns a simple list into hours of clerical work.
03 / DECAY
Static lists go stale
Administrators change. Agencies close. New operators launch. Within months, yesterday’s research becomes today’s bounce list.
What you get
A ready-to-work market, not a raw directory export.
Each row combines license data, decision-maker context, visible demand-generation signals, and a ranked reason to reach out.
verified agency records across 24 live states. One signed client pays for a year of this.
The file's job is to get you that client — every agency in your market, the owner's name, and a plain note on why they're worth a call this week. Delivered as a clean CSV that drops into Excel, Sheets, or your CRM — your states on signup, Hot 10 every week, refreshed weekly. New states land on All-Access at no extra cost as they are verified and added — and on Done-For-You, this database is the weapon we work for you.

After that: the Hot 10 for your states every Monday, fully refreshed files every week, and new states as they are verified and added — included on All-Access, addable on DIY for $75/mo each.

Before you subscribe.
Where can I buy a list of home care agencies?
OwnerFlight tracks 2,860 home care agencies across 24 live states — Florida, Texas, California, New York, Pennsylvania, Ohio, Washington, Illinois, Arizona, North Carolina, Georgia, Massachusetts, Virginia, New Jersey, Michigan, Tennessee, Missouri, Maryland, Wisconsin, Minnesota, Colorado, Alabama, Alaska, and Hawaii — built for businesses that sell into home care. Subscribe to the database for $299/month, or take Done-For-You ($800/month) and we run the outreach and book the calls for you.
How much does OwnerFlight cost?
Done-For-You is $800 per month, or $8,000 annually paid upfront (saving $1,600 versus monthly billing; annual subscriptions renew each year): we email the agency owners in your market, work every reply, and book calls on your calendar — if the first launched service month produces zero positive replies, monthly DFY clients get the next service month free and prepaid annual clients carry the same zero-reply protection (annual prepay already includes two months free). The DIY database is $299 per month for any 3 states you choose, cancel anytime. Extra states are $75 per month each, and All-Access — every live state — is $499 per month. Whatever rate you start at is yours for as long as you stay subscribed — it never goes up on you. The posted DFY checkout does not automatically charge a separate setup fee; any additional fee requires your approval before payment. A lower-commitment option is the Pilot Flight: $400 one time for one full outreach flight in your market — the full $400 can be credited manually toward qualifying DFY started within 14 days, and if the flight and a free second flight both produce zero positive replies, the $400 is refunded. There is no per-record charge.
What information is included for each agency?
Agency name, city, street address, phone, website, state license number, owner or administrator name, Google rating and review count, Instagram handle and recent activity, online-booking signal, a 0-100 priority score, a tier (HOT, WARM, NURTURE, or COLD), and a plain-English reason for the score. Fields that cannot be verified are left blank rather than estimated.
Who is OwnerFlight for?
Any business that sells into home care: home care and senior care marketing specialists, software and EHR vendors, staffing platforms, billing and RCM firms, answering services, consultants, and franchise development firms. It is not a consumer directory and it is not for agencies looking to be listed.
What does Done-For-You (DFY) include?
We email the licensed home care agency owners in your market using the verified contacts in our database, work every reply, and book calls on your calendar. You approve the outreach angle before launch, replies are handled and reported on the agreed campaign schedule, and you receive a weekly sent / replies / booked report. Full database access for your market is included. Guarantee: monthly DFY receives a free second month if the first fully launched month generates zero positive replies; prepaid annual DFY carries the same zero-reply protection (annual prepay already includes two months free).
How is this different from Apollo or ZoomInfo?
Broad B2B platforms are built to cover every industry. OwnerFlight is built around one vertical and includes license context plus senior-care-specific prospecting signals — such as visible Instagram activity and online-booking gaps — that broad databases typically do not carry.
See the full side-by-side: OwnerFlight vs Apollo and ZoomInfo →
What format do I receive?
A clean CSV that can be opened in Excel or Google Sheets and imported into most CRM and outreach platforms.
How often do I receive updates?
After we verify a completed checkout and confirm the selected markets, data files are emailed manually — any 3 states you choose on DIY, every live state on All-Access. After that you receive the Hot 10 brief for your states every Monday and fully refreshed, re-verified files every week. New states are added as they are verified: All-Access includes them at no extra cost, and on DIY you can add a state anytime for $75/mo.
How does priority scoring work?
Every agency gets a 0–100 priority score from our own scoring model. It weighs the signals that say an agency is ready to buy — how established it is, whether it can take an online booking, how visible it is online — and every row shows the reason for its score in plain English. Scores land in tiers: HOT, WARM, NURTURE, COLD. The recipe itself is ours; what it produces is what you see in the public preview.
What counts as a trigger?
Triggers include a newly issued license, a meaningful Google rating change, social activity going quiet, or a visible conversion gap such as no online booking. Each Hot 10 entry includes the change, when it was detected, and a suggested outreach angle.
Which states are covered?
Twenty-four states are live: Florida (104 agencies), Texas (126), California (114), New York (114), Pennsylvania (111), Ohio (122), Washington (123), Illinois (111), Arizona (107), North Carolina (120), Georgia (225), Massachusetts (123), Virginia (129), New Jersey (121), Michigan (118), Tennessee (120), Missouri (122), Maryland (151), Wisconsin (116), Minnesota (106), Colorado (116), Alabama (120), Alaska (78), and Hawaii (63) — 2,860 agencies in total. More states are in build and are added only once verified, at no extra cost.
Can I cancel?
Yes. Both tiers are month-to-month and you can cancel anytime. Whatever rate you start at is yours for as long as your subscription stays active — it never goes up on you.

Why I built this
Built by the person who got tired of the scavenger hunt.
Prospecting into home care used to mean a dozen open Maps tabs, one state license lookup after another, and lists that were stale before the first call — hours of hunting before a single conversation. So I built the file I couldn't buy: every licensed agency scored, every owner named, refreshed every week. OwnerFlight is that file, and the outreach service I wished had come with it.

Why bought lists fail
You have bought this list before. It did not work then either.
The standard list-buying experience — pay per record, get a spreadsheet, start dialing — breaks in the same three places every time.
01 / STALE
Dead on arrival
Most lists are scraped once and resold for years. Agencies close, rebrand, move, and change administrators — and the spreadsheet never hears about any of it. Your first week of outreach becomes a cleanup project.
02 / NO OWNER
A name, not a person
A business name and a front-desk number is not a lead. Without the owner or administrator — cross-checked against the state license record — your reps pitch whoever answers the phone and hope it travels upward.
03 / NO TIMING
No reason to call today
A flat list treats a fast-growing agency and a dormant one as identical rows. Nothing in it says who has a visible problem a marketer can fix this week — so every call starts cold, in every sense.
Here is what the Florida market actually looks like when you verify it record by record — this gap is the opportunity, and it is invisible in a bought list:
Online booking
19 of 32
Florida agencies verified so far show an online booking path — the other 13 verified are phone-only in a market where families shop online first. Statewide verification is still in progress; we publish only what we've checked.
Instagram
99 of 102

Straight answers, before you subscribe.
Where can I buy a list of home care agencies?
OwnerFlight is a subscription database of licensed home care agencies, built for marketing agencies: 2,860 verified records across 24 live states — owner names, direct phones, and license numbers where verified, plus ratings, booking and social signals, and a priority score on every record. It is $299/month, and the $400 Pilot Flight proves it in your market before you subscribe. Twenty-four states are live — 2,860 agencies, Florida to Colorado — and DIY includes your choice of three states ($299/month); All-Access includes all 24 states ($499/month) with no hidden per-record fees.
Are these leads exclusive to my agency?
No — and we would rather say that plainly. OwnerFlight is a shared subscription database: every member works from the same verified file. What members compete on is speed and follow-up, and the weekly Hot 10 and its timing signals are built to give you that edge. If a vendor promises exclusive leads at this price, ask how many times they have sold them.
What information comes with each agency?
Thirteen core fields: agency name, city, street address, phone, website, state license number, owner or administrator, Google rating and review count, Instagram handle and recent activity, online-booking signal, priority score, tier, and a plain-English reason for the score. Fields that can’t be verified are left blank, never estimated. One honest gap: this file doesn’t include email addresses. Verified owner emails live in DFY — the tier where we do the emailing for you. DIY is owners, phones, licenses and scores, built for calling.
How fresh is the data?
The Florida file was verified record by record in October 2026, against state license records and each agency's live web presence. The full database is re-verified and refreshed every week, and the Hot 10 brief goes out every Monday with the highest-priority accounts and what changed.
Which states are covered?
Twenty-four states are live — 2,860 agencies, Florida to Colorado — and DIY includes your choice of three states ($299/month); All-Access includes all 24 states ($499/month). Whatever rate you start at is yours for as long as you stay subscribed.

Broad B2B platforms are built to cover every industry. OwnerFlight publishes flat prices with self-serve Stripe checkout: a $400 one-time Pilot Flight, Done-For-You at $800/mo, and the DIY database at $299/mo (any 3 states), plus All-Access — every live state — at $499/mo. Apollo and ZoomInfo sell per-seat contracts, typically quote-only.

How it works
Three steps. No integration project, no cookie arguments.
Tracking is deliberately simple: a personal partner code, logged in our subscriber registry at signup. If a signup names your code, it is yours — permanently, and auditable any time you ask.
01
Get your partner code
Email us and tell us about your audience. We issue your personal code and walk you through the file, so you only promote what you have actually seen.
02
Share the data or the offer
Publish the market findings, share the $400 Pilot Flight, host a session, or link the database — always with your code attached and your commission disclosed.
03
Earn every month, for life
Commissions tally monthly and pay out via Stripe once your balance passes $100 — 10% on DIY subscriptions ($29.90/mo each), 25% on DFY clients ($200/mo each) — and keep paying for as long as each subscriber stays subscribed.
Partner conduct
Simple rules, enforced.
The whole product is trust in data. Partners protect that — and their commission — by following three rules. The full terms arrive with your partner code, before you promote anything.
Rule 01
Honest claims only
Cite the published brief and the live coverage — 24 states are live today. Never promise states, features, or results we have not shipped.
Rule 02
Disclose the commission
A simple “I may earn a commission” line wherever you promote. FTC basics — it protects you, us, and your audience's trust in both.
Rule 03
No spam, ever
No purchased lists, no mass unsolicited outreach, no posting your code where you do not have permission to promote. One spam complaint ends the partnership.

## Florida Home Care 2026 Data Brief — https://santi856.github.io/ownerflight/brief.html

The State of Florida Home Care — 2026 Data Brief | OwnerFlight
OwnerFlight
← The database
2026 Data Brief · Florida
The State of Florida Home Care, in numbers.
We analyzed 102 licensed Florida home care agencies — their websites, booking paths, social presence, and Google profiles. The headline: this is a large, licensed, paying market that is almost completely invisible online.
Data collected & verified October 2026 · OwnerFlight research
19 / 32
verified agencies offer any online booking
Booking status is verified agency by agency against each agency's own site. Of the 32 verified so far, 19 offer online booking and 13 are phone-only. The rest are still being verified — we publish only what we've checked.
99 / 102
have no findable Instagram presence
Just 3 agencies in the entire dataset have an Instagram profile we could find. The channel families actually browse is essentially empty.
10
median Google reviews per rated agency
Ratings average a strong 4.8★ — but on a median of 10 reviews, one unhappy family moves the number. High ratings, thin proof.
102
licensed agencies, verified one by one
Built from Florida license records, cross-checked against each agency's live web presence. Unverifiable fields are left blank — never estimated.
Where the agencies are
The dataset concentrates in Florida's major metros — the same metros where private-pay demand and agency competition are highest:
Jacksonville · 14
Miami · 13
Orlando · 8
Tampa · 7
Altamonte Springs · 7
St. Petersburg · 6
Kissimmee · 5
Orange Park · 5
What this means if you sell marketing to home care agencies
The booking gap is a web & intake pitch, pre-written
13 of the 32 agencies verified so far
can't take a booking or consultation request online. Every one is flagged individually in the database — that's not a cold list, it's 13 warm reasons to call, with more verifying every week.
Social silence is a content pitch with no competition
When
97% of a market has no Instagram presence
, the first agency in each city that shows up consistently owns the feed by default. The database flags exactly who is dark.
Thin reviews are a reputation pitch with urgency built in
A 4.8★ average on a median of 10 reviews is a number one bad month can wreck. Agencies know it, even if they haven't fixed it — the database carries rating and review count on every record so the conversation starts specific.

One full outreach flight in your market — first 10 only, refund-backed. Zero positive replies and a second flight is free; still zero and the $400 is refunded in full.
Methodology
This brief is drawn from the OwnerFlight Florida database (October 2026): licensed home care agencies identified from Florida license records and cross-checked against each agency's public website, Google Business profile, and social presence. Online-booking and Instagram figures reflect what could be found on each agency's public web presence at verification time; records that could not be verified were left blank rather than estimated. The full database — owner/administrator names, phones, license numbers, ratings, booking and social signals, and a 0–100 priority score with a plain-English reason per record — is refreshed weekly, with a weekly Hot 10 of the agencies showing the freshest buying triggers. Florida was the first market. Twenty-three more states are live now.
